questions.question: Select the grammatically correct sentence.

options.text: An intricate dance of neurotransmitters in the synaptic cleft plays the crucial role in neural communication.
An intricate dance of neurotransmitters in a synaptic cleft plays a crucial role in neural communication.
The intricate dance of neurotransmitters in the synaptic cleft plays a crucial role in neural communication.
The intricate dance of neurotransmitters in a synaptic cleft plays the crucial role in neural communication.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. The intricate dance of neurotransmitters in the synaptic cleft plays a crucial role in neural communication.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• This sentence uses the definite article **"the"**, which is appropriate when referring to a specific noun that is known or has been previously mentioned in context. Here, "the synaptic cleft" refers to a specific space involved in neural communication.
 
• The use of the phrase **"plays a crucial role"** is grammatically correct and conveys the intended meaning clearly.
 
• The subject-verb agreement is correct: **"The intricate dance... plays"**. The singular subject requires the singular verb form "plays."

Correct sentence: *The intricate dance of neurotransmitters in the synaptic cleft plays a crucial role in neural communication.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** Incorrect because it uses "the crucial role," which implies there is only one specific crucial role in all contexts, which may not be accurate here.
 
• **Option 2:** Incorrect because it uses "a synaptic cleft," which implies any random synaptic cleft, not a specific one crucial to the context.
 
• **Option 4:** Incorrect because it uses "a synaptic cleft" instead of "the synaptic cleft," which fails to indicate a specific known space in the context of neural communication.
</ul

questions.question: Select the grammatically correct sentence.

options.text: If you want to have a sound working knowledge of Japanese, you must read this book.
If you want to have an sound working knowledge of Japanese, you must read this book.
If you want to have sound working knowledge of the Japanese, you must read this book.
If you want to have a sound working knowledge of the Japanese, you must read this book.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. If you want to have a sound working knowledge of Japanese, you must read this book.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence is grammatically correct because it uses the article **"a"** appropriately before the phrase **"sound working knowledge."**
 
• The word **"sound"** is an adjective that starts with a consonant sound, so the article **"a"** is correct.
 
• Option 2 is incorrect because it uses **"an"**, which is used before words that start with vowel sounds.
 
• Options 3 and 4 are incorrect because the phrase **"of the Japanese"** is awkward in this context; it is better to say **"of Japanese"** when referring to the language.

Correct sentence: *If you want to have a sound working knowledge of Japanese, you must read this book.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Articles are used before nouns or noun phrases to specify whether the noun is definite (**"the"**) or indefinite (**"a" or "an"**).
 
• **"A"** is used before words that start with consonant sounds, while **"An"** is used before words starting with vowel sounds.
 
• In this sentence, **"sound"** starts with a consonant sound, making **"a"** the correct article.

questions.question:

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of 'clarify' in the sentence given below.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Illustrate**.

__
 
• The word **"Clarify"** means to make something easier to understand by providing more details or simplifying the explanation. (स्पष्ट करना)

 
 
• **Example:** The teacher clarified the difficult concept by using diagrams and simple language.
 
 
 
• **"Illustrate"** means to explain or make something clear by using examples, pictures, or diagrams. (चित्रण करना)
 
 
• **Example:** The professor illustrated the concept of gravity by showing a video of falling objects.
 
 
 
• Hence, the word "illustrate" is synonymous with "clarify" in the given context.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Illustrate**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Last **(अंतिम): Refers to the final or concluding part of something.

 
 
• **Example:** The last chapter of the book provided a surprising twist.
 
 
 
• **Help **(मदद): To assist or aid someone in accomplishing a task.
 
 
• **Example:** She helped her friend solve the math problem.
 
 
 
• **Confused **(उलझन में): Refers to a state of not being able to understand or think clearly.
 
 
• **Example:** He was confused about whether to take the bus or the train.

questions.question:
Change the following sentence into positive degree.

Sushma is one of the smartest girls in the class.

options.text: Few girls in the class are as smart as Sushma.
Sushma is the smart girl of the class.
Sushma is smarter than any other girls in the class.
No other girl is as smart as Sushma.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. Few girls in the class are as smart as Sushma.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence uses a **superlative degree**, "Sushma is one of the smartest girls in the class."
 
• To change the sentence into **positive degree**, we need to express the comparison in a way that compares Sushma's intelligence to the other girls without using superlative or comparative forms like "smartest" or "smarter."
 
• Option 1, "Few girls in the class are as smart as Sushma," correctly expresses the idea in the **positive degree**.
 
• Other options either use incorrect grammar or fail to convert the sentence into **positive degree**.

Correct Sentence: *Few girls in the class are as smart as Sushma*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Degrees of Comparison:**

 
 
• **Positive Degree:** Describes a quality without making comparisons.

 **Example:** Few girls are as smart as Sushma.
 
• **Comparative Degree:** Compares two entities.

 **Example:** Sushma is smarter than any other girl in the class.
 
• **Superlative Degree:** Highlights the highest degree of quality among three or more entities.

 **Example:** Sushma is one of the smartest girls in the class.
